F6 [Nit] review-b: The live path audits the lockfile of the caller's working directory, not the lockfile of this repository. scripts/audit-gate.mjs:88 calls `execFileSync` with no `cwd` option. Rationale: the gate, run from a directory that holds the base lockfile (a copy of 7bc4a4e0), printed `critical=0 high=4 moderate=6 low=1 info=0` and exited 1. The same gate exits 0 at the repo root. A run from `/` gave exit 2, and a run from `tests/` audited the repo root (exit 0). A clean lockfile in another directory would give a false exit 0. The plan commands run at the repo root, so the normal path is not affected. Disposition: note. Pass `cwd` as the repo root, taken from `import.meta.url`, to `execFileSync`.

F7 [Nit] review-b: No test covers the timeout branch. scripts/audit-gate.mjs:18 fixes `TIMEOUT_MS` at 120000, and tests/audit-gate.test.ts has no hanging-binary case. Removal of `timeout: TIMEOUT_MS` (line 91) or of the `err.signal` check (line 95) keeps all 17 tests green (read from the code; not run). Rationale: the code works. A copy of the script text with a timeout of 800 ms and a `sleep 30` child gave exit 2 and `audit unavailable` after 0.83 s. A child that leaves a grandchild on the pipe gave the same result. A child that prints without end gave exit 2 after 0.03 s, because of the 1 MiB `maxBuffer`. Disposition: note. Make the timeout overridable in a test, or accept the gap.

F8 [Nit] review-b: The integrity claim for the manual Chrome for Testing download gives no URL, size, or digest. measure/runs/chore_dependency_refresh_20261121/jr-green-6987ed50.log:57-60 says the archives were `integrity checked with unzip -t`. That command checks the CRC of each member. It finds a damaged or cut-off download, and it does not prove the origin. Rationale: my own check shows the claim is true (see the evidence entries on Chrome for Testing). Disposition: note. Add the two URLs and the md5 values from those entries to plan.md T3.

AUDIT_GATE_PNPM probes (live path, no --input): the values /nonexistent, /bin/true, /bin/false, /bin/echo, /bin/sh, `/`, `x; touch /tmp/ag-inj-marker`, `$(touch /tmp/ag-inj-marker2)`, a backtick form, and `/bin/echo && touch /tmp/ag-inj-marker4` all gave exit 2 with `audit unavailable`. None of the four marker files exists afterwards. scripts/audit-gate.mjs:88 calls execFileSync with a constant argument list and no shell, so the value names a program and nothing else. The override is documented at scripts/audit-gate.mjs:11-13, tests/audit-gate.test.ts:11-13, and the plan.md T1 r2 evidence. An empty value falls back to `pnpm`.

Residual risk of the override: a process that controls the gate environment can name a stand-in program that prints a clean document, and the gate then exits 0. The same process can already put a fake `pnpm` first on PATH, so the override adds no privilege. The `pnpm` on this host is the bash shim /home/daniebo/.local/bin/pnpm, which runs `exec npx -y pnpm` and so fetches an unpinned pnpm. That is host state outside the diff, and it existed in round 1.

A HEAD request to each official object returned the same content-length and an x-goog-hash md5 equal to the local md5 (uH0+6HvvYbe6EGxA2g4Cgw== and BJJDSoRgfLrepeAnvl4bTA==). unzip -tq printed `No errors detected` for both archives.

Chrome for Testing install: a Python zipfile check compared the SHA-256 of every zip member with the extracted file. ~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1255 has 301 files (432681149 bytes), and chromium_headless_shell-1255 has 287 files (293841839 bytes). The check found 0 missing files, 0 different files, and 0 mode differences. The only extra entries are the Playwright marker files DEPENDENCIES_VALIDATED and INSTALLATION_COMPLETE and directory names. The older builds 1228 and 1234 are kept.

Judgment of the integrity claim: the claim is true, and the install is authentic as far as the origin is. The command unzip -t alone proves only that the archives are undamaged. The md5 match against the origin object shows that the local archives are the official ones, and the hash check shows that the extracted trees equal the archives. The x-goog-hash md5 is the bucket's own digest and not a signature, so the trust root is Google's bucket over HTTPS. A normal playwright install uses the same class of trust: it downloads builds/cft/<version> from cdn.playwright.dev (coreBundle.js:34355-34357); I did not check that installer for a digest check. The browser cache lies outside the repo and the lockfile, so it is machine state. No security finding applies to the install itself; F8 covers the record gap.
